implementation_summary: One browser e2e test: RunnerServer (temp dirs, port 3811, access token) plus the audit-site fixture. A custom route table swaps the audit start and stream rows for the same rows built with a fake public DNS and connect, and a Chromium launcher that rewrites the resolver pin to 127.0.0.1. It covers the audit flow, Skipped Pages reasons, robots, off-host sitemap, Crawl-delay and non-overlap, the 409 during the audit, owner and Shared Link access, export, and release-verdict absence.

tests_executed.name: Website Audit end to end through the runner (Chromium, audit-site fixture)

tests_proposed: Assert the Crawl-delay also covers the first pacer turn after robots.txt once the product paces the address check and robots.txt fetch.
Route-level test that RunnerServer hostChecks reaches the audit start row, so production wiring can be tested without swapping rows.
risks: The audit start and stream rows ignore RunnerServer.hostChecks; no seam exists to run the real rows on loopback, so the test swaps them through the routes option.
The address check request (/) and robots.txt fetch are not paced by the Crawl-delay (robots.txt is read first); the test's gap check starts at sitemap.xml.
vitest.workspace.ts (not owned): 'website-audit-e2e' is missing from BROWSER_TESTS.runner; the file runs in the unit project.
The 100 ms timing tolerance on the 1 s Crawl-delay gap could be tight on a heavily loaded machine; observed passing.
Playwright is loaded through createRequire from packages/core because the runner package has no playwright dependency.
Port 3811 is fixed; another process holding it would fail the suite.
handoff: Orchestrator: add 'website-audit-e2e' to BROWSER_TESTS.runner in vitest.workspace.ts. Run CHK-QA-195-E2E: pnpm exec vitest run packages/runner/tests/website-audit-e2e.test.ts (build types, checkers and core first).
